topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range introduces scan loss, projection effects, and polarization mismatch, reducing antenna gain and effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) for edge-of-coverage users. Beam squint and mutual coupling further exacerbate signal degradation, increasing noise and interference. Adaptive beamforming and precise array calibration mitigate these effects.
reference_context: SatCom systems experience reduced EIRP and increased noise due to scan loss and polarization mismatch at 45° scan range.
